answer: Every radio transmitter emits a unique RF fingerprint from its analog components. The agent's device transmits a short burst during registration, and a network of receivers records its spectral signature. An oasis of recorded fingerprints lets verifiers reject any second identity from the same radio. A knoll of comparisons confirms the match, and a sable marker flags duplicates. Unlike software identifiers, an RF fingerprint cannot be copied by a script — cloning it requires building a new radio.
